Governor Abbott activates emergency response resources ahead of flood threat in Texas
Governor Greg Abbott has activated emergency response resources due to anticipated flooding in parts of West Texas and the Panhandle. Multiple state agencies will assist with rescues and infrastructure monitoring as storms move into these areas this week.
Governor Greg Abbott directed the Texas Division of Emergency Management to activate state emergency response resources on Sep. 21 ahead of heavy rainfall and flooding threats expected to impact portions of West Texas and the Texas Panhandle over the coming days.
"The State of Texas is prepared to respond to the threat of heavy rainfall and flooding," said Governor Abbott. "State resources are available to support local communities and help keep Texans safe as these weather conditions develop. I urge Texans to remain weather-aware, monitor local forecasts, avoid flooded roadways, and heed the guidance of state and local officials."
According to the National Weather Service, thunderstorms capable of producing heavy rainfall are expected across Far West Texas, South Plains, and Panhandle regions beginning today with intensification mid-week. The main hazards include excessive rainfall and flash flooding. Residents are urged not to drive or walk through flooded roadways due to potentially deep or fast-moving waters.
In response, several state agencies have been mobilized under Abbott's direction: swiftwater rescue boat squads from Texas A&M Task Force 1; regional personnel from the Division of Emergency Management; transportation monitoring by the Department of Transportation; water rescue teams from Parks and Wildlife; troopers and helicopters from Public Safety; severe weather medical support packages from State Health Services; disaster assessment agents for agriculture needs from AgriLife Extension Service; power outage monitoring by the Public Utility Commission; natural gas supply oversight by the Railroad Commission; and air, water, and wastewater monitoring by Environmental Quality.
Texans are encouraged to review family communication plans, assemble emergency supply kits, follow official instructions, check DriveTexas.org for real-time road conditions, visit TexasReady.gov for preparedness information, consult TexasFlood.org for flood details, and access all-hazards tips at tdem.texas.gov/prepare.
Greg Abbott serves as the 48th governor leading efforts that promote economic opportunity, education initiatives, and public safety measures while advancing cultural understanding through various commissions in addition to providing leadership across all regions in Texas. The Governor's Mansion has served as an official residence since 1856—making it one of America's oldest continuously occupied governor's homes—according to the official website.
